rules.statement: Don't report a "Generated by"/AI-tool attribution line in a pull request title or description as a review finding; the `Commit attribution` check already fails it, so first read the current description and that check's latest result.
rules.why: The template's Test-CommitAttribution.ps1 check fails such a line and reruns when the description is edited; tooling may append the line and remove it seconds later, so a finding based on the description as opened is often stale.
rules.check: Before raising an attribution finding, look at the current PR description and the latest `Commit attribution` run; if the check enforces it, don't report.

rules.statement: Don't ask for a CI step or MSBuild target that checks a packed .nupkg contains the file named by `PackageIcon`; NuGet pack already fails when the icon is missing or not in the package.
rules.why: Pack fails with NU5019 when the icon file is missing and NU5046 when PackageIcon names a file the package doesn't contain, and the Definition of Done build packs every shipping project on every pull request.
rules.check: When a diff adds or changes PackageIcon/icon packing, don't request an extra verification; only report an actual wrong path that would break pack.

rules.statement: In a file the project template manages, treat the "Kept from this repository's own … when it adopted the project template" line as the split marker for template updates: repository-specific lines and notes belong below it, and don't ask to move them above it.
rules.why: The template update script splits the file at that marker, merging everything above with the template's next version and keeping everything below as is; a note moved above would be taken as an edit to the template's part.
rules.check: Before reporting that a comment sits under a stale or unrelated "Kept from…" heading, recognize it as the template marker; flag only repository-specific content placed above it.

rules.statement: In Python scripts, discard tuple-unpacked values that are never read with `_` instead of binding them to a named variable.
rules.why: A named but unused variable suggests the logic depends on that value when it doesn't.
rules.check: Look for names bound in tuple unpacking that are never read afterward.
